ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, the line $y=-2x+3$ intersects the $y$-axis at point $A$ and the $x$-axis at point $B$. Point $P$ is a moving point on segment $AB$. Perpendicular lines are drawn from $P$ to the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis, and the feet of the perpendiculars are denoted as $C$ and $D$, respectively. Connect $CD$. When $CD$ is minimized, what is the value of $PA\cdot PB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $PC\perp OB$, $PD\perp OA$, and $\angle DOB=90^\circ$, \\
it follows that quadrilateral $OCPD$ is a rectangle. \\
By connecting $OP$, we have $CD=OP$. \\
Therefore, when $OP\perp AB$, $OP$ is at its shortest, meaning $CD$ is also at its shortest. \\
Since $y=-2x+3$, \\
when $x=0$, $y=3$, and when $y=0$, $x=\frac{3}{2}$. \\
Thus, $A(0,3)$ and $B\left(\frac{3}{2},0\right)$, \\
which means $OA=3$ and $OB=\frac{3}{2}$, \\
and so $AB=\sqrt{OA^2+OB^2}=\sqrt{3^2+\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2}=\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{5}$. \\
$\tan\angle OBA=\frac{OP}{PB}=\frac{OA}{OB}=2$, \\
Letting $PB=x$, then $PO=2x$. \\
Therefore, $x^2+4x^2=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2$, \\
Solving this, we find $x=\frac{3}{10}\sqrt{5}$, \\
Hence, $PB=\frac{3}{10}\sqrt{5}$ and $PA=AB-PB=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}-\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{10}=\frac{6}{5}\sqrt{5}$, \\
Therefore, $PA\cdot PB=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{10}\times \frac{6\sqrt{5}}{5}=\boxed{\frac{9}{5}}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system xOy, O is the origin, the x-axis points to the right, and the y-axis points upward; a straight line slanting downward to the right intersects the y-axis and the x-axis at A and B respectively. Point P is on the oblique line segment AB; from P draw a perpendicular to the x-axis, with foot C; from P draw a perpendicular to the y-axis, with foot D; CD is connected in the figure. It can be seen from the figure that O, C, P, D form a rectangle, and CD and OP are the two diagonals of this rectangle. Reasoning: Because OCPD is a rectangle, CD=OP. To make CD minimal is equivalent to making OP minimal. When P moves on AB, when OP is minimal, OP should be perpendicular to AB, that is, P is the foot of the perpendicular from O to AB. From the straight line y=-2x+3, we can obtain: when x=0, y=3, so A=(0,3), OA=3; when y=0, x=3/2, so B=(3/2,0), OB=3/2. Thus in the right triangle AOB, AB=sqrt(3^2+(3/2)^2)=sqrt(9+9/4)=3sqrt(5)/2. When OP is perpendicular to AB, OP is the altitude on the hypotenuse AB of the right triangle AOB. Using the right-triangle hypotenuse altitude relation, PA·PB=OP^2; also by the area relation OP=(OA·OB)/AB, so PA·PB=OP^2=(OA^2·OB^2)/AB^2. Substituting OA=3, OB=3/2, AB=3sqrt(5)/2, gives PA·PB=(9·9/4)/(45/4)=81/45=9/5.

推理：因为 OCPD 是矩形，所以 CD=OP。要使 CD 最小，就等价于使 OP 最小。P 在 AB 上移动时，OP 最小时，OP 应垂直于 AB，即 P 是 O 到 AB 的垂足。
由直线 y=-2x+3 可得：当 x=0 时，y=3，所以 A=(0,3)，OA=3；当 y=0 时，x=3/2，所以 B=(3/2,0)，OB=3/2。于是直角三角形 AOB 中，AB=sqrt(3^2+(3/2)^2)=sqrt(9+9/4)=3sqrt(5)/2。
当 OP 垂直 AB 时，OP 是直角三角形 AOB 斜边 AB 上的高。利用直角三角形斜边高关系，PA·PB=OP^2；又由面积关系 OP=(OA·OB)/AB，所以 PA·PB=OP^2=(OA^2·OB^2)/AB^2。代入 OA=3，OB=3/2，AB=3sqrt(5)/2，得 PA·PB=(9·9/4)/(45/4)=81/45=9/5。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, the line $y=-2x+3$ intersects the $y$-axis at point $A$ and the $x$-axis at point $B$. Point $P$ is a moving point on segment $AB$. Perpendicular lines are drawn from $P$ to the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis, and the feet of the perpendiculars are denoted as $C$ and $D$, respectively. Connect $CD$. When $CD$ is minimized, what is the value of $PA\cdot PB$?
raw_record.answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $PC\perp OB$, $PD\perp OA$, and $\angle DOB=90^\circ$, it follows that quadrilateral $OCPD$ is a rectangle. By connecting $OP$, we have $CD=OP$. Therefore, when $OP\perp AB$, $OP$ is at its shortest, meaning $CD$ is also at its shortest. Since $y=-2x+3$, when $x=0$, $y=3$, and when $y=0$, $x=\frac{3}{2}$. Thus, $A(0,3)$ and $B\left(\frac{3}{2},0\right)$, which means $OA=3$ and $OB=\frac{3}{2}$, and so $AB=\sqrt{OA^2+OB^2}=\sqrt{3^2+\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2}=\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{5}$. $\tan\angle OBA=\frac{OP}{PB}=\frac{OA}{OB}=2$. Letting $PB=x$, then $PO=2x$. Therefore, $x^2+4x^2=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2$. Solving this, we find $x=\frac{3}{10}\sqrt{5}$. Hence, $PB=\frac{3}{10}\sqrt{5}$ and $PA=AB-PB=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}-\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{10}=\frac{6}{5}\sqrt{5}$. Therefore, $PA\cdot PB=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{10}\times \frac{6\sqrt{5}}{5}=\boxed{\frac{9}{5}}$

Point P is on the oblique line segment AB; from P draw a perpendicular to the x-axis, with foot C; from P draw a perpendicular to the y-axis, with foot D; CD is connected in the figure. It can be seen from the figure that O, C, P, D form a rectangle, and CD and OP are the two diagonals of this rectangle.
Reasoning: Because OCPD is a rectangle, CD=OP. To make CD minimal is equivalent to making OP minimal. When P moves on AB, when OP is minimal, OP should be perpendicular to AB, that is, P is the foot of the perpendicular from O to AB.
From the straight line y=-2x+3, we can obtain: when x=0, y=3, so A=(0,3), OA=3; when y=0, x=3/2, so B=(3/2,0), OB=3/2. Thus in the right triangle AOB, AB=sqrt(3^2+(3/2)^2)=sqrt(9+9/4)=3sqrt(5)/2.
When OP is perpendicular to AB, OP is the altitude on the hypotenuse AB of the right triangle AOB. Using the right-triangle hypotenuse altitude relation, PA·PB=OP^2; also by the area relation OP=(OA·OB)/AB, so PA·PB=OP^2=(OA^2·OB^2)/AB^2. Substituting OA=3, OB=3/2, AB=3sqrt(5)/2, gives PA·PB=(9·9/4)/(45/4)=81/45=9/5.
